subject: Q2 QBR: Release Readiness — cross-org launch contingencies & owners
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: sam.wells@nimbus.ai, priya.shah@cloudpartner.io
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 QBR: Release Readiness — cross-org launch contingencies & owners

Team —

As we lock the Q2 agenda for the upcoming QBR, I want to run a focused readiness checkpoint for the release slated for 2027-04-02. Goal: ensure leadership has a single slide that lists launch-ready, known risks that need mitigation before the board readout, and clear owners for each contingency.

Summary (high level):
- Current target date: 2027-04-02 (hard ship window for hosted and dedicated)
- Primary concerns: infra scalability at peak, marketplace onboarding dependencies, and quantization regressions on the latest model bundle
- Ask: please review your section below and confirm concrete mitigations + readiness percent by EOD tomorrow.

Initial ask/owners:
- Product (Laura): finalize rollout scope and canary cohorts; confirm comms plan to customers.
- Engineering (Karthik): resolve the KV cache corruption observed in staging and validate failover policy.
- Runtime/Infra (Markus): confirm autoscale threshold adjustments and capacity backstop for first 48 hours post-launch.
- Ops/Release (Tessa): validate the canary deployment steps and rollback runbook; coordinate DocuSign flow for any emergency SLA addenda.

Attached: Q2_QBR_launch_matrix.xlsx (matrix with owners and impact levels) and canary-plan-v2.pdf

Please reply inline. We’ll synthesize into the QBR slide deck on Friday 2027-03-19.

Thanks —
Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick updates from Product:

- Rollout scope: scoped to hosted API and Redwood Dedicated first; Private (VPC) customers will be on a delayed wave (+2 weeks) unless they opt in. This reduces blast radius for the board window.
- Canary cohorts: initial cohort = 10 external customers + 3 Redwood internal teams (growth, search, ops). Will expand to 50 after 24h if metrics look good.
- Comms: draft customer email ready; will route to legal for one minor change today.

Readiness: 78% — remaining items:
- Need confirmation from Markus on capacity backstop (blocking expanding cohort)
- Need SRE sign-off on latency SLI thresholds for the canary dashboard (Karthik, can you confirm ETA?)

Subject: Re: Q2 QBR: Release Readiness — cross-org launch contingencies & owners

Jordan / team —

Quick operational note on the autoscale/capacity ask:

- We can provide a short-term capacity backstop by pre-warming an extra 12-GPU pool in us-west for the first 48 hours. Cost/backstop tradeoff is acceptable for the board window.
- Risk: there is a known rare failure mode in the current kernel selection path under very short sequences that can degrade latency by ~50ms on P99. We have a patch candidate but it requires a canary run on a subset before we flip at scale.

Mitigations proposed:
1) Pre-warm the pool (Markus owner) — ETA: 24h to confirm procurement and scheduling.
2) Hold the kernel flip behind canary; do not roll to Dedicated until +48h stable.
3) If we see P99 spike > 200ms, autoscale target will increase concurrency cap and we will shift traffic to the warm pool.

I will update the matrix and add explicit roll-forward/rollback criteria in the canary plan.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Runtime & Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Jordan / all —

Short engineering status:

- KV cache corruption that appeared in staging earlier this week is traced to an errant async flush when resizing shards. We have a fix in a feature branch and unit/integration tests are green. Need a staging canary run against the latest model bundle to validate under realistic load. ETA for canary run: 24-36 hours (start Fri afternoon PST).
- Blocker: one of the external test customers we planned for the canary (Nimbus Analytics) reports their SDK compatibility test failing on our gRPC endpoint — Sam, thanks for flagging. Can your team confirm whether the failure is a cert pinning issue or a proto mismatch?

Readiness estimate: 64% (pending successful canary + Nimbus verification).

Karthik

Karthik / Team —

Quick follow-up from Nimbus: the SDK failure is a mutual TLS handshake problem driven by our cert rotation last week. We see a client-side disconnect during TLS renegotiation when connecting to the gRPC endpoint. We can provide logs and the rotated cert chain if that helps.

Action we can take today: share the cert bundle and run an integration test from our side; if you can whitelist the rotated CA chain in staging it should clear the test.

Planning note: we are on board with being in the initial canary cohort but prefer the Dedicated wave only after the +48h stability window.

—Sam
